markets.name: goods
markets.summary: People sell everyday things, new or used.
markets.description: Things are handed over and paid in person, or shipped when the price is one either side could lose; not motor vehicles or homes.

markets.name: home-cleaning
markets.description: Cleaners are paid by the visit, and often come every week.

markets.name: home-gardening
markets.summary: Gardeners mow, prune, plant and care for people's gardens.
markets.description: Each visit or job is paid once it is done, and gardeners often come every week or two; not landscaping or building, which are paid in stages, nor felling trees.

markets.name: home-repair
markets.summary: Repairers do plumbing, electrical and handyman jobs in people's homes.
markets.description: Each job is paid once it is done; not renovations paid in stages. Garden work is home-gardening, and cleaning is home-cleaning.

markets.name: language-exchange
markets.summary: Two people practise each other's language, taking turns.
markets.description: Partners meet online or in person, with no money between them; paid lessons are tutoring. For adults.

markets.name: software
markets.summary: Developers build and fix software, AI, data and automation, remotely.
markets.description: Building and fixing software of every kind, AI, data, automation and security work included, delivered remotely; not design alone, video or hardware. Pay piece by piece, each piece once delivered, so neither side risks much.

markets.name: sports-coaching
markets.summary: Coaches teach a sport or fitness, one on one or in groups.
markets.description: Coaching is in person or online, paid by the session, the hour or a pack of sessions; the student is whoever arranges the coaching, often a parent, who stays present for a child's session in person. Desk subjects and chess are tutoring.

markets.name: stays-free
markets.summary: Hosts give guests a couch or a room for free.
markets.description: Hosts ask only for good company: no tasks and no money between them; a bed for help is stays-work. For adults.

markets.name: stays-work
markets.summary: Hosts give guests a bed, and often meals, for their help.
markets.description: Guests help on a farm or in a hostel, with building, or by sitting a house or pets, with no money between them; never childcare, and help for a cause with no bed is volunteering. For adults.

markets.name: tours
markets.summary: Local guides show a group around, paid on the day.
markets.description: The tour may be a food, walking, history or nature tour, or any other kind, and is paid per person or, for a private tour, for the whole group. For adults.

markets.name: tutoring
markets.summary: Tutors teach school subjects, languages, chess and other desk subjects.
markets.description: Lessons are online or in person, paid by the lesson, the hour or a pack of lessons; the student is whoever arranges the lessons, often a parent, who stays present for a child's lesson in person. Sport and fitness are sports-coaching; practising a language for free is language-exchange.

markets.name: volunteering
markets.summary: Volunteers give their time to cleanups, food banks, events and good causes.
markets.description: Organizers offer a spot to help, in person or online, and volunteers ask for one: cleanups, food banks, community events, nature, animal shelters, and remote help for a cause, such as translating or writing. Not a bed for help, which is stays-work, and not caring for children or for people who need care. In person it is for adults only, since strangers meet; online it is open to anyone.
